extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. It covers 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains, and 4 task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was assembled by aggregating existing multilingual speech datasets (MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14) and collecting new speech recordings for sentences from the FLoRes machine translation benchmark to create the Fleurs dataset.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The FLEURS dataset is noted to be complete at more than 97%, with some missing recordings that may be addressed in a second version.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include the FLoRes machine translation benchmark, read audiobooks from LibriVox (MLS), European Parliament sessions (VoxPopuli), CoVoST-2, Minds-14 e-banking spoken data, and text from Wikipedia and CommonCrawl.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African or South Asian, which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated; Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting given the discrepancy between the richness of the input signal (speaker, domain, recording conditions) and the small number of output labels.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages; Catalyzing research in universal speech representation learning.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings). Updates will be made on our platform.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For the speech retrieval task, the pool of transcription candidates for each language is augmented with 100k sentences from Wikipedia. For the Minds-14 dataset, monolingual datasets are merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.
